# Draft:Howard P. Rockey

Howard Primrose Rockey (June 3, 1886- May 27, 1934) was a writer in the United States. His stories were published in magazines and he wrote novels. His short story "Li Ting Lang, Chinese Gentleman" was published in the December 1916 edition of The Green Book Magazine and was adapted into the 1920 film Li Ting Lang.
Life and career
The son of Henry Chester Rockey and Mary Berry Rockey, Howard Rockey was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania on June 3, 1886. He attended the Thaddeus Stevens School of Observation as a child. He was educated at the Drexel Institute and Temple University. From 1903-1907 he was a reporter for the The Philadelphia Inquirer.
From 1927-1930 he worked for the Lord & Thomas and Logan Advertising Agency out of their offices in Philadelphia.
Rockey died on May 27, 1934 in Manhattan.
